relevance.rationale: JOIN CONFIRMED against the document's front matter and the preprint number, matching the registry's independently verified note. IMPORTANT READING NOTE FOR ANY LATER TRIAGE: a naive `grep -i dilogarithm` over the extracted text returns ZERO hits and would suggest the corpus's ~15 Φ_b citations on this key are all miscited. That conclusion would be WRONG. The document introduces the non-compact quantum dilogarithm under the symbol s(P), not Φ. On p. 4–5 it poses the functional equation s(P+p)/s(P) = 1/(1 + e^{iPq/ħ}), gives the solution as the contour integral s(P) = exp[(1/4)∫_{−∞}^{∞} e^{iPqξ/ħ}/(sinh πξ · sinh πθξ) · dξ/ξ] with the ξ=0 singularity circled from above, then derives the ratio form s(P) = s_θ(u)/s_θ̂(v̂) with θ̂ = −1/θ and s_θ(u) = exp[(1/2i) Σ_n (−1)^{un}/(n sinh πnθ)]. Those are precisely the objects the corpus formalises in `FaddeevPhiBRealIntegral.lean` (integral representation), `PhiBProd.lean` and `FaddeevRatioPeriodic.lean` (ratio / product form), `PhiBProdProductConvergence.lean` and `FaddeevQuantumDilogarithm.lean`. Those citations are LOAD-BEARING AND CORRECT. ONE LOOSE Ref: TAG. `FaddeevPhiFullUniqueness.lean:43` writes '-- Ref: [faddeev1995] … — uniqueness of Φ_b'. The document proves a Schur-type Lemma (an operator commuting with the algebra is a multiple of unity) and exhibits A solution to the functional equation — it states no uniqueness theorem for s(P), and in fact remarks 'It is not evident, that this r(P) is generated by u and v̂ as it should'. The file's own prose is more accurate than its tag: it says the strip-growth bound is 'the physical asymptotic condition that Faddeev AND KASHAEV use to single out Φ_b', i.e. the intended source is the joint work registered under a different key, not this one alone. The file is otherwise exemplary — it explicitly labels instStripGrowth and hNF as carried axioms rather than proved theorems.
